parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: A nucleus of caesium-137 ($^{137}_{55}\text{Cs}$) decays by emitting a $\beta^-$ particle to produce a nucleus of an element X and an antineutrino. The decay is represented by $$^{137}_{55}\text{Cs} \rightarrow ^{Q}_{S}\text{X} + ^{P}_{R}\beta^- + ^{0}_{0}\bar{\nu}.$$
parts.text: State the number represented by each of the following letters.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the class (group) of particles that includes the $\beta^-$ particle and the antineutrino.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A particle Y has a quark composition of $ddd$ where $d$ represents a down quark.

A particle Z has a quark composition of $\bar{u}d$ where $\bar{u}$ represents an up antiquark.
parts.text: Show that the charges of particles Y and Z are equal.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain which particle is a meson and which particle is a baryon.
